48.original: Greetings and welcome to the Athenaeum Astrologicum. Perhaps you were drawn by fate to this place of learning─or perhaps you wish to know more of fate itself?

49.original: Do you wish to know more of fate?

52.original: Then you were wise to come hither. For in the stars are written the fates of every woman and man on Hydaelyn.

53.original: So you say, yet here you are. You need only learn to open your eyes and see the answers which lie above us in the boundless firmament.

54.original: It was there in the stars that I read a <hex:02080FE905FF06776F6D616EFF046D616E03> would call upon the Athenaeum this very day. A <hex:02080FE905FF06776F6D616EFF046D616E03> who would play an important role in <hex:021A020203>my<hex:021A020103> own life.

55.original: Ah, but my apologies. Even the most skilled reader cannot scry a name from the heavens. Would you be so kind as to give me yours, so that I might know who is to be my newest protégé?

56.original: Give Jannequinard your name and become his protégé?

59.original: <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. Well... I was not expecting that. But what is a name, but an attempt by our begetters to wield power over the lives of their sons and daughters? Lives whose paths have already been foretold! In a sense, that is.

60.original: My name is Jannequinard de Durendaire and I am an astrologian for the Holy See. Remember that name, for it shall echo forevermore in the annals of Ishgardian history. Well...it will once I put it there. Once <hex:021A020203>we<hex:021A020103> put it there!

61.original: Well...er... That was awkward. It would not be entirely true if I said this was the first time my offer had been spurned today... But Twelve be damned, I was certain you were the <hex:02080FE905FF06776F6D616EFF046D616E03> from my vision!
